title: JRE 2285 - Andrew Schulz
guestBio: Andrew Schulz is a stand-up comic, actor, and podcaster. He's the host of the "Flagrant" podcast with Akaash Singh, and the "Brilliant Idiots" podcast with Charlamagne Tha God. Look for his new special "Life" on March 4 on Netflix.
tldr: Andrew Schulz discusses his comedy special 'Life' dropping on Netflix March 4 and what inspired the material
Conversation about the state of stand-up comedy and how comedians navigate sensitive topics in 2024
Andrew talks about hosting multiple podcasts including Flagrant with Akaash Singh and Brilliant Idiots with Charlamagne
Discussion of comedy as a tool for social commentary and pushing boundaries
Andrew shares insights about the comedy podcast space and audience evolution
Banter about performing, touring, and building a fanbase independent of traditional media
recap:
Joe sits down with Andrew Schulz on JRE 2285 to talk comedy, podcasting, and his new Netflix special 'Life' hitting the platform March 4. Schulz has established himself as one of the more prolific voices in comedy and podcasting, running both the Flagrant podcast with Akaash Singh and Brilliant Idiots with Charlamagne Tha God, giving him reach across different corners of the comedy world.

The conversation touches on how stand-up comedy has evolved and the pressure comedians face when trying to be honest on stage. Andrew talks about the balance between being entertaining and being authentic, which is central to his comedy approach. They discuss the power of comedy as a medium for social commentary and how comedians have always been the ones willing to say what others won't.

Schulz shares his perspective on building an audience through podcasting and touring rather than relying solely on traditional comedy club bookings or TV appearances. The podcast space has become a major vehicle for comedians to build independent fanbases and maintain creative control. Andrew emphasizes how important it is for comedians to connect directly with their audience rather than being filtered through network executives or venue owners.

The discussion includes insights into what makes a comedy special work and how the Netflix platform has changed the landscape for stand-up. Schulz talks about the creative process behind 'Life' and what he wanted to accomplish with the special. They also touch on the collaborative nature of comedy, particularly how working with other comedians and podcast hosts has shaped his perspective and material.

quotes: Stand-up comedy is one of the last places where you can actually say what you think
The podcast space has given comedians the freedom that traditional media never allowed
My special 'Life' is about being honest about where we are as a society and as individuals
You have to connect with your audience directly, not through some filter
Comedy has always been the canary in the coal mine for what society is really thinking
